methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Editorial: New study envisions Virginia workforce changes with AI - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: A statewide workforce study examining AI's impact suggests awareness of transformation but frames workers as recipients of change rather than builders of capability, signaling toward platform-driven shallow adoption rather than grassroots technical depth.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Richmond's young workforce facing 'AI pressure' indicates metro hub anxiety about keeping pace with deeper technical demands, reinforcing the concentration pattern where capability expectations cluster in urban centers while leaving rural areas outside the urgency frame.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-backed community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia represents distributed capacity-building originating from local institutions rather than platform deployment, offering a counter-signal to concentration if training includes hands-on AI/data skills rather than just awareness.

signals.title: Virginia lawmakers study AI risks and potential new regulations - WTVR.com
signals.signal_reading: Lawmakers studying AI risks and regulations without visible parallel investment in distributed literacy or training infrastructure signals governance happening above rather than alongside capability development, potentially freezing adoption through uncertainty while depth remains concentrated.

signals.title: Roanoke College president: Virginia’s future workforce depends on fixing the path from college to career - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College president advocating to fix the college-to-career pathway signals institutional commitment to distributed workforce preparation in a non-metro region, suggesting potential for peer-network skill transfer if curriculum includes deep technical training rather than surface-level platform use.
